text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Wednesday:
- Denmark will preside over the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) starting January 1, when Switzerland's year in the chairmanship comes to an end.
- Nearly 48,000 people employed in Switzerland's metal industry and in agriculture will not receive wage increases for 1997.
- Elektrowatt subsidiary Kummler & Matter will lay off some 30 employees over the next few months when it shuts down several branches. The company has suffered a huge decline in orders.
- Oerlikon Precision Laser SA in Gland will lay off 22 of its 26 employees due to financial difficulties.
- Percy Barnevik, president of the board of ABB, was elected to General Motor's board of directors.
- Employees in Switzerland's graphic industry will not get wage increases in 1997. Journalists earning minimum salaries will receive 0.5 percent raises.

- Some 34 percent of people in the German-speaking region of Switzerland now fear losing their jobs, compared to 11 percent in 1995, according to a recent study. In western Switzerland, the figure jumped to 48 percent from 20 percent in 1995.
- The Swiss Federal Railways are issuing 10 million tickets with advertisements printed on them in an effort to stop counterfeiting.

- Swiss Justice Minister Arnold Koller, 63, was due on Wednesday to be elected by parliament to the largely symbolic post of Swiss president for 1997, a one-year position that rotates among the seven members of the cabinet. He will succeed Economics Minister Jean-Pascal Delamuraz.
